name: house edge doubled
guard: Step 7 (Multiplier Derivation) must reject a doubled edge. Step 7 DERIVES the served multiplier's numerator as (1 - HOUSE_EDGE) * 10000, so the pin becomes 9800/basisPoints and no captured winning multiplier matches. QA 2026-09-09 P1-6: round 1 hardcoded 9900 here, at which point this declared guard stopped guarding — the run still flipped, but via Steps 10/16/20/21, and the registry named a step that no longer fired.

name: lower bound flipped to exclusive

replace: const inBand = roll > p.lower && roll < p.upper;

name: upper bound inclusive, win rule only (one-line)
find: const inBand = roll >= p.lower && roll < p.upper;
replace: const inBand = roll >= p.lower && roll <= p.upper;
guard: Step 13 (Anti-Circularity) must reject an inclusive upper bound in diceWin ALONE: the 10,000-point tally calls diceWin and now counts the upper-bound grid point, so it disagrees with the unchanged half-open closed-form discreteWinCount (first band {0, 92.37}: tally 9238 vs closed form 9237). No settled bet lands on an upper bound, so Steps 6/15 do NOT see this — the tally cross-check is what catches the one-line change.

name: upper bound inclusive, CONSISTENT model (the pre-E13 release)
find: const inBand = roll >= p.lower && roll < p.upper;
replace: const inBand = roll >= p.lower && roll <= p.upper;
find2: const inBand = Math.max(0, Math.min(RANGE, hi) - Math.max(0, lo));
replace2: const inBand = Math.max(0, Math.min(RANGE, hi + 1) - Math.max(0, lo));
guard: With BOTH diceWin and discreteWinCount made inclusive-upper the model is internally consistent: no settled bet lands on an upper bound (P = 1/10,000 per draw) so Steps 5/6 pass, and the Step 13 tally agrees with the closed form so anti-circularity passes. It is caught two ways: Step 15 ASSERTS the per-bet effective edge as an EXACT INTEGER identity (100*winCount*9900 === 99*RANGE*basisPoints; the old form was a 1e-12 float band, retired 2026-09-09 because its worst-case noise was 5.06e-13), which the inclusive model breaks by making winCount 100W+1, so `npm run verify` returns NOT PROVABLY FAIR; AND the E13 boundary-probe mocha vectors fail (roll == upper must LOSE) — five mocha tests, all resting on the same half-open premise whose only external source is E13. This is EXACTLY the regression the original release shipped; before Step 15 asserted the edge per bet, `npm run verify` returned 21/21 and only the mocha vectors rejected it. Runner is mocha (expect failing); the verify-side rejection is exercised by the one-line variant above.

name: settlement rounding switched from half-EVEN to half-up

if (r > HALF_UNIT) q += 1n;
  else if (r === HALF_UNIT && (q % 2n) === 1n) q += 1n;     // exact tie → round to even
guard: Step 8 (Credit Arithmetic) must reject half-up settlement. The capture contains 274 exact 8-dp ties; under half-up every one of them rounds up, so the rule stops reproducing the operator's credits. This is the mutation that proves the two-stage rule's ROUNDING MODE is evidence and not decoration.

name: upper bound inclusive in the CLOSED FORM only (discreteWinCount)
find: const inBand = Math.max(0, Math.min(RANGE, hi) - Math.max(0, lo));
replace: const inBand = Math.max(0, Math.min(RANGE, hi + 1) - Math.max(0, lo));
guard: Step 15 (Odds Boundary & Effective Edge) must reject a winning-region count that is not 100*W. The mirror image of the diceWin-only mutation: here the win RULE is untouched (so every settled bet still reproduces) and only the grid tally moves to 100*W+1. The integer identity 100*winCount*9900 === 99*RANGE*basisPoints breaks immediately. This is the mutation that demonstrates the identity is doing work rather than being algebraically vacuous — the algebra holds only while winCount == 100*W, which is exactly the claim E13 licenses.

name: Pass-1 uniformity forged to a PERFECT fit (chi2 = 0, p = 1.0)
guard: Step 16 (Simulation Pass 1) must reject a chi-squared in the LOWER tail. This is the isolated, single-file form of the fabricated-Pass-1 counterexample in tests/structural-forgeries.json: it changes NOTHING the step re-derives (the stored pValue is still exactly the recomputed pValue, the depth is still pinned, the model block is untouched), so under the pre-2026-09-09 predicate `uniP >= ALPHA` it PASSED — p = 1.0 is as far from rejection as a p-value gets. The screen is TWO-SIDED at ALPHA_SCREEN, half the level in each tail: the upper tail is the real test and the lower tail rejects a 2,000,000-draw histogram that sits closer to its expectation than sampling allows. That is a test with a size, and it is counted in the error budget (S1) — unlike the equality-based 'perfection proves fabrication' rules removed for D4, which had none.

name: convergence standard error forged (the D3 counterexample)
guard: Step 16 (Simulation Pass 1) must validate every PLOTTED standard error, not merely check that it is a number. EXECUTED COUNTEREXAMPLE, client QA 2026-09-10 (D3): change the first convergence checkpoint's SE from 0.03130348064353228 to 123456, re-pin the artifact, and the suite returned a Full Pass — the step asserted only Number.isFinite. Chart comparison could not see it either, because src/chart.ts clamps the +/-5*SE ribbon to the plot box (Math.min(ymax, ...)), so both bands draw identically. The SE is now RECOMPUTED from (n, rtp, wins, m) — the integer win count being recoverable from the published RTP, since every win pays the same multiplier — and compared bit-for-bit.

name: convergence RTP moved off any integer win count
guard: Step 16 (Simulation Pass 1) must reject a published running RTP that no integer win count produces. A convergence point is the producer's return for an integer win count in [0, n]; 0.97911 at n=1000 with m=1.98 implies 494.5 wins, which is not a count, and the stored count 493 reconstructs to 0.976140000000006, which the published figure is not. recoverWinCount rejects it; the stale SE (left at the honest 493-win value) rejects it a second time.

name: convergence RTP off an integer win count by 0.1 — INSIDE the old reconstruction cap, with the SE recomputed to match
guard: Step 16 (Simulation Pass 1) must reject a fractional win count that sits INSIDE the old quarter-win cap, and must not be rescued by the forger recomputing the derived fields. Client QA round 5 (2026-09-11, blocker 1), in single-file form: 0.976338 at n=1000 with m=1.98 implies 493.1 wins, only 0.1 from the integer 493, so the round-4 rule rounded it to 493 and accepted it; the SE is moved in the same edit to 0.03130348126972461, exactly what convergenceSE(1000, 0.976338, 493, 1.98) returns, so the D3 standard-error check reconciles and cannot be what rejects it. What rejects it is the forward reconstruction: 493 wins accumulate to an RTP of 0.976140000000006, and the published figure is 0.1 wins away from that — far outside the derived arithmetic tolerance at this count. The end-to-end effective-edge form is tests/forgeries/fractional-win-count.mjs.

name: schema-2 artifact missing a required schema-2 field (runs cell count n1)
guard: Step 16 (Simulation Pass 1) must score an artifact by ITS OWN declared schema, and a schema-2 declaration carries obligations: the runs test's cell counts (runs, n1, n) so runsZ is re-derivable rather than trusted. This artifact IS schema 2; deleting the n1 cell count leaves schemaVersion=2 in place but strips a field the schema requires, so runsStructureOk cannot re-derive runsZ from the counts and Step 16 fails. The artifact is re-pinned after the edit, so the hash cannot be what catches it (client QA 2026-09-10, D3/D7).

name: rejection window widened to the whole uint32 domain (modulo bias reintroduced)
guard: Step 5 (Roll Recomputation & Draw Bias Bound) must reject a draw whose accepted window is not a whole number of ranges. Setting maxFairFor(range) to the full 2^32 domain removes the modulo-bias rejection: drawBiasBound then sees MAX_FAIR = 4294967296 with 4294967296 % 10000 = 7296 (not a whole number of ranges) and a worst-case bias ~1.70e-9, above the 2^-32 (~2.33e-10) ceiling, so the DICE-08 half of Step 5 fails. This is the ISOLATING mutation for DICE-08: it introduces genuine modulo bias while leaving every captured recomputation identical — no captured bet's first uint32 chunk reaches the discarded [4294960000, 2^32) tail (rejection probability 1.70e-6 per chunk), so the recomputation half of Step 5 stays green and only the bias-bound half fires. It is exactly the bias no amount of live recomputation can see, which is why the bound is arithmetic rather than a live statistic.

name: M-LIVESERIAL captured rolls sorted into value order — live-sample serial independence destroyed
replace: return { ...parsed, bets: [...parsed.bets].sort((a: any, z: any) => a.roll - z.roll), sha256, path };
guard: Step 22 (Live-Sample Serial Independence) is a numbered step that reports INFO and cannot fail: it returns PASS or INFO, never FAIL or FLAG, so this entry is an INFORMATIONAL SIGNAL and `npm run mutate` counts it separately, never as a kill. Sorting the 6,700 captured rolls into value order makes the draw sequence monotonic, so lag-1 autocorrelation -> +1 and the Wald-Wolfowitz runs test collapses to two runs — exactly the serial dependence this informational screen exists to report — and Step 22 reports INFO. The step is verdict-neutral (policy INFORMATIONAL, 2026-09-29: not counted, Full Pass preserved), so the non-zero exit never comes from Step 22. It comes from the reproduction gate (the changed Step 22 status/detail no longer match the committed verification-results.json) and, measured 2026-10-02, from Step 19: its recomputed report figures differ from the committed ones in the settlementResidual group once the bets are reordered. Step 4 is order-independent (it re-sorts each epoch by nonce and checks the nonce SET), and every per-bet step keeps each bet(seed, clientSeed, nonce, roll) tuple intact, so no other step fails. What the entry shows is that the screen is not vacuous — a serially dependent stream does reach INFO — not that Step 22 can fail.

name: M-C3i one uncaptured setting (win chance 50.03 %) priced 2 pp below the claim, table + record regenerated
find: acc.add(`win chance ${(bp / 100).toFixed(2)}%`, BigInt(bp) * BigInt(PAYOUT_NUMERATOR), BigInt(RANGE) * BigInt(bp));
replace: acc.add(`win chance ${(bp / 100).toFixed(2)}%`, BigInt(bp) * BigInt(bp === 5003 ? PAYOUT_NUMERATOR - 200 : PAYOUT_NUMERATOR), BigInt(RANGE) * BigInt(bp)); // MUTATION
guard: Step 15 (DICE-19), FIXPASS2 C3(i): one setting misses the published figure by more than the band and nothing else changes. The price of win chance 50.03 % (bp 5003; no captured bet has that band width, normal or inverted) is lowered to 9700/bp where the RTP table prices it, so that one setting returns 97 %, 2 pp below the flat 99 % claim. With the table re-written and re-pinned and the record re-emitted (regen), the run must end RTP FIGURE OVERSTATED, exit 5, Step 15 OVERSTATED: no earlier check may turn it into exit 1 or 2. Without regen the committed table no longer matches (Step 15 FAIL, exit 1). Dice has no paytable file: the price is the formula 9900/bp, so the cell is lowered at the one place the table reads it.

name: M-C3ii published figure raised to 99.25 % in the claim source, table + record regenerated

Every one of the 9,800 settings (99 %) is then 0.25 pp below a 99.25 % claim. With the table and record regenerated the run must end RTP FIGURE OVERSTATED, exit 5, Step 15 OVERSTATED.
